videos.title: Two young humpback whales at the bow

notes: Only the operator's own site was read (about 25 pages); no captcha, bot check or 403 was met. The site links no YouTube or Vimeo channel (footer links are Facebook, X, Pinterest, Instagram and Tripadvisor only), so the single video is an .mp4 the operator hosts itself, posted in their 'Mugged by two juveniles' news item (27 December 2025); the file answers with video/mp4. Left out: a YouTube embed (3qkUML0lziU) on the news post 'Fantastic video footage courtesy of Into the Wild Photography', because the site credits it to Michael Smith of Into The Wild Photography. Also left out: images credited to others, namely the Jens Assmann photography article image (2020/03/whale-watching-hervey-bay-article-by-jens-assmann-photography.jpg) and the Escape Travel feature image (2022/09/sues-whale-watching-adventures-escape-travel-website2.jpeg); 2025/05/2TB0E38-scaled-scaled.webp, whose file name looks like a stock agency reference; banners and header backgrounds (freedom-banner-home2.jpg, boat-header-background.jpg, freedom-whale-watch-hero-home.jpg, about-us-header-background3.jpg, boat-header-background3.jpg and the slideshow files); the Tripadvisor, Google five-star, Best of Queensland 2025 and Ecotourism Australia badge graphics; a guest testimonial portrait (testimonials-xiao.jpg); and very small thumbnails (whale-tail-A.jpg, closeupspyhop-1-1.jpg and similar). Logo is the full-size navy horizontal logo in the site header (1820 by 446 px, PNG). heroImage is offered as a better wide setting shot (whale, guests and the Fraser Island coast, per the site's own caption); the site's current home hero is Freedom-spyhop-fotor-2924x1948px.png, a 5.6 MB PNG, so the lighter .webp copy of the same photo is used in the gallery and in the facts file. The cruise page itself carries eleven older photos from about 2012 to 2014 (the operator's own whale and deck photos; the gallery alt text calls some of them guest photos); the first six by size are listed after the three newest cruise photos from the 2026 cruise photo album, which belongs to the same cruise. The Private Charters trip has no page of its own, so its photos come from the 2026 album (boat, Pelican Island, deck and saloon), a 2020 wedding charter photo and two photos from the 2014 summer cruise album (previous owners), which a person may want to drop. Image URLs were not downloaded. Header requests (no download) on the logo, the home hero, the new hero choice, four other photos and the video all answered 200; the rest are recorded as served in the page HTML.
